units: probability
interpretation: P(H2): the repository's operational AGI definition is already satisfied by a system existing on 2026-10-06.
reason_for_distribution: H2 fails on the definition's 'reliable/automate' and 'very wide range' clauses: >50% of successful 4-8h agent tasks at OpenAI still need human intervention; Anthropic and METR both judge the frontier model 'not close to substituting' for research scientists and 'likely unable to fully and reliably automate R&D for projects spanning multiple weeks'; OpenAI's own model is below its 'High' AI-self-improvement threshold. Evidence for H2 is real but narrower (superhuman bounded optimisation, OSWorld 85%, cyber 'Critical', a few open maths problems) plus insider claims (Brockman, Huang) that are commercially conflicted. Residual 10% covers definitional slack ('approximately expert-level').

units: human-expert hours (50% success, METR TH1.1-style SWE/ML/cyber suite) at 2026-10
interpretation: Frontier 50% autonomous task horizon on today's date.
reason_for_distribution: METR measured early Mythos Preview (Mar 2026) at >=16h (95% CI 8.5-55h) and says >16h is unreliable on its suite; Anthropic reports Opus 4.6 at ~12h (Feb 2026); Mythos 5 (Jun) and Mythos 5.1/GPT-6 Astra (Sep) are described as on-trend. Rolling 16h forward ~6 months at a ~4-5 month doubling gives ~35-45h; centred lower (32h) because the >16h numbers are lower bounds of an unreliable range and METR flagged saturation. Wide p95 reflects that no robust post-May number exists.

units: months per doubling of the 50% horizon at 2026-10 compute growth
interpretation: Current doubling time of the reliable task horizon.
reason_for_distribution: TH1.1: 89 days (2.9 mo) since 2024, 131 days (4.3 mo) since 2023, 196 days (6.4 mo) long-run. Anthropic reports ~4 months. AI Futures (Apr 2026) use 4-4.5. v0.5.1 used 7 months (the long-run rate) and was too slow (see backtest). Median 4.5 deliberately sits above the 2024+ fit because long tasks lack human baselines and METR warns of saturation.

units: ratio of each doubling's duration to the previous one (<1 = superexponential)
interpretation: Pre-AGI AI-R&D feedback and the 'infinite horizon at AGI' argument shorten successive doublings.
reason_for_distribution: AI Futures' median parameters imply mildly superexponential horizon growth; METR's Kwa notes the AGI-implies-infinite-horizon argument. Against: Anthropic finds Mythos 5 is a level shift with no further slope acceleration ('inconsistent with compounding acceleration'); Epoch finds the 2024 acceleration is a one-off reasoning-model break. Mode 0.96 = mild; high 1.08 allows sub-exponential.

units: 50% task horizon (human-expert hours) at which the SWE/ML gate is met
interpretation: Definitional threshold: horizon needed for reliable autonomous expert work.
reason_for_distribution: 80% horizons run ~5x below 50% horizons (Mythos: 16h vs 3.1h). 'Reliable' month-long expert projects (80% horizon ~167h, METR's headline month) => 50% horizon ~800-1000h. AI Futures' Automated Coder uses an 80% horizon of ~1 work year (=> ~10,000h at 50%), the upper tail. Lower tail (~100h) covers readings of the definition under which current systems are close.

units: extra horizon doublings needed for the weakest broad domains to catch up
interpretation: Lag of non-verifiable, open-ended and perception-heavy work behind SWE horizons.
reason_for_distribution: METR (Jan 2026): visual computer-use horizons were 40-100x (5-7 doublings) below SWE, now largely closed (OSWorld-Verified 85%). Open-ended research judgement still lags (Princeton shadow evaluation: agent papers rejected; Anthropic: 'large performance gaps persist' in choosing goals). Expressed in doublings so the lag scales with the actual pace of progress instead of being a fixed calendar delay.
